claim: IAM role manager is an optional account setting that automatically provisions the IAM roles that AWS services need to act on your behalf; it is available in select AWS service consoles and works by applying a role template, a definition of a role's trust policy and permissions for a service and use case. The roles it creates behave like any other role: you can view, edit or delete them.

evidence.quote: Many AWS services depend on IAM roles to perform actions on your behalf. IAM role manager is an optional account setting that automatically provisions such roles, so you don't have to set them up yourself.
Role manager is available in select AWS service consoles, listed in AWS service consoles that support role manager on this page.
Role manager works by applying a role template, a definition of a role's trust policy and permissions for a service and use case.
IAM roles created by role manager behave like any other role you create. You can view, edit, or delete them.
Today, AWS announces the general availability of role manager, a capability in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) that automatically sets up the IAM roles your AWS services need.
